findings.title: [P1] Define a compatible `renderError` method before invoking it
findings.body: The new catch block calls `this.renderError(error)`, but `SearchController` declares no such method, and no definition exists anywhere in the repository (a repo-wide search finds only the new call site). TypeScript will report TS2339 ("Property 'renderError' does not exist") on this added line, and if type checking is bypassed, any `api.search` rejection or `render` exception is replaced by `TypeError: this.renderError is not a function`. Since error rendering is the entire purpose of this change, the error path is broken in every scenario that exercises it.

findings.title: [P2] Ignore failures from superseded searches before rendering them
findings.body: Every call to `search` unconditionally aborts the in-flight request (`this.active?.abort()` on line 21) before starting a new one. With an abort-aware `api.search` (the `signal` argument implies it is), the superseded request's promise rejects with an `AbortError`, which the new catch now renders as a user-facing error — and because the older rejection can settle after the newer request has rendered, it can clobber the fresh results with a spurious error view. The catch should ignore `AbortError` (or verify the failing request still owns `this.active`) before rendering.

findings.title: [P2] Re-throw failures after rendering them, or document the swallowed rejection
findings.body: Before this change, an `api.search` rejection or a `render` exception rejected the promise returned by `search`. The new catch resolves successfully whenever `renderError` returns, so any caller using `await search(...)`, `.catch(...)`, or rejection-based retry/reporting silently loses the original failure — contradicting the PR's stated intent of "preserving existing contracts". No in-repo caller currently depends on this (the class has no callers here), but the observable async contract of a public method changed unintentionally; re-throwing after rendering (or documenting the fire-and-forget behavior) preserves it.
